explicit_requirements: Cancelling an active subscription must change its status to cancelled.
After cancellation, the user must no longer have access to premium features.
Repeated cancellation must not crash the application.
Cancellation must leave the subscription in a consistent cancelled state without premium access.
ambiguities: Cancellation behavior for subscription states other than active or already cancelled is unspecified.
The supplied context describes a premium_access state field but does not establish how access to premium features is enforced beyond that field.

scenarios.name: Active subscription becomes cancelled
scenarios.behavior: Cancel an active subscription and check that its status becomes cancelled.
scenarios.reason: The original task directly requires this state transition. The repository context identifies status as the subscription state field.

scenarios.name: Cancellation removes premium access
scenarios.behavior: Cancel an active subscription with premium access and check that premium_access becomes false. Distinguish this state observation from any separate claim about enforcement of access to premium features.
scenarios.reason: The original task explicitly requires removal of premium access. The context identifies premium_access as the corresponding boolean field, but supplies no separate feature-access enforcement interface.

scenarios.name: Repeated cancellation remains safe and consistent
scenarios.behavior: Cancel the same subscription again after it has been cancelled and check that the application does not crash, its status remains cancelled, and premium access remains disabled.
scenarios.reason: The original task explicitly requires safe repeated cancellation and a consistent cancelled state without premium access. The context says each HTTP request creates fresh state, so separate requests alone would not establish repeated cancellation of the same subscription.
